answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 56% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the canyon registry records each claim and the raven audit publishes every slash. A farm must therefore either lie, which the knoll graph proves on replay, or recruit 46 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 10 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
